title: DLMF 25.14 Lerch’s Transcendent: If s is not an integer then \left|\operatorname{ph}a\right|<\pi ; if s is a positive integer then a\neq 0,-1,-2,\dots…
summary: DLMF 25.14 Lerch’s Transcendent: If s is not an integer then \left|\operatorname{ph}a\right|<\pi ; if s is a positive integer then a\neq 0,-1,-2,\dots…
body: NIST DLMF section 25.14 (Lerch’s Transcendent) says: "If s is not an integer then \left|\operatorname{ph}a\right|<\pi ; if s is a positive integer then a\neq 0,-1,-2,\dots ; if s is a non-positive integer then a can be any complex number. For other values of z , \Phi\left(z,s,a\right) is defined by analytic continuation. This is the notation used in Erdélyi et al. ( 1953a , p. 27) . Lerch ( 1887 ) used \mathfrak{K}(a,x,s)=\Phi\left(e^{2\pi ix},s,a\right) . The Hurwitz zeta function \zeta\left(s,a\right) (§ 25.11 ) and the polylogarithm \operatorname{Li}_{s}\left(z\right) (§ 25.12(ii) ) are special cases: Here the prime signifies that the term for n=m-1 is to be omitted. In the case s=1 we have For hypergeometric function F see 15.2(i) . With the conditions of ( 25.14.1 ) and m=1,2,3,\dots , For these and further properties see Erdélyi et al. ( 1953a , pp. 27–31) . with \max(-\Re{a},-1)<\sigma<0 . This Mellin–Barnes integral representation is used in Olde Daalhuis ( 2024 ) to obtain large \left|z\right| asymptotic approximations for \Phi\left(-z,s,a\right) . In the special case s=m an integer these asymptotic approximations simplify" Equation 25.14.1 on the page has alt text "{\Phi\left(z,s,a\right)\equiv\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{n}}{(a+n)^{s}}},". Equation 25.14.2 on the page has alt text "\zeta\left(s,a\right)=\Phi\left(1,s,a\right),". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
